The tenth season of the American [[science fiction]] television series ''[[The X-Files]]'' commenced airing in the United States on January 24, 2016, on [[Fox Broadcasting Company|Fox]]. The season consists of six episodes and concluded airing on February 22, 2016. When Fox initially announced the string of episodes, the network referred to them collectively as an "event series".<ref>{{cite web |title=The Next Mind-Bending Chapter is Coming |url=http://www.fox.com/the-x-files/article/the-next-mind-bending-chapter-is-coming |publisher=[[Fox Broadcasting Company|Fox.com]] |access-date=January 26, 2016 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150326085806/http://www.fox.com/the-x-files/article/the-next-mind-bending-chapter-is-coming |archive-date=March 26, 2015 |df=mdy-all}}</ref> After their release, Fox began referring to the episodes collectively as "season 10" on their website,<ref>{{cite web |title=The X-Files |url=http://www.fox.com/the-x-files |publisher=[[Fox Broadcasting Company|Fox.com]] |access-date=January 28, 2016 |archive-date=January 1, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160101212237/http://www.fox.com/the-x-files |url-status=dead }}</ref> as did streaming sites like [[Amazon Prime]] and [[Hulu]],<ref>{{cite web |title=The X-Files Season 10 |url=https://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B019EG1WC0?ref_=aiv_dp_season_select |publisher=[[Amazon.com]] |access-date=January 28, 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Watch The X-Files |url=http://www.hulu.com/the-xfiles |publisher=[[Hulu]] |access-date=January 28, 2016}}</ref> and myriad critics.<ref>For a small sampling, see:
*{{cite web |title=The X-Files – Season 10 |url=https://www.metacritic.com/tv/the-x-files/season-10 |work=[[Metacritic]] |access-date=January 23, 2016}}
*{{cite web |title=The X-Files: Season 10 |url=https://www.rottentomatoes.com/tv/the-x-files/s10/ |work=[[Rotten Tomatoes]] |access-date=January 23, 2016}}
*{{cite web |last1=Soto |first1=Kaly |title='The X-Files' Season 10, Episode 2: That's More Like It |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2016/01/25/arts/television/the-x-files-season-10-episode-2-review-founders-mutation.html |website=[[New York Times]] |access-date=January 28, 2016 |date=January 25, 2016}}
*{{cite web |title=The X-Files |url=https://www.tvguide.com/tvshows/the-x-files/episodes/100536/ |website=[[TV Guide]] |access-date=January 28, 2016}}
*{{cite web |title=The X-Files – Episode Guide |url=http://tvlistings.zap2it.com/tv/the-x-files/episode-guide/EP00080955?aid=zap2it |work=[[Zap2it]] |access-date=January 28, 2016}}</ref>

The season, which takes place fourteen years after the [[The X-Files season 9|ninth season]] (2001{{en dash}}02) and seven years after the film ''[[The X-Files: I Want to Believe]]'' (2008), follows newly re-instated [[Federal Bureau of Investigation]] (FBI) agents [[Fox Mulder]] ([[David Duchovny]]) and [[Dana Scully]] ([[Gillian Anderson]]) as they learn more about the existence of extraterrestrials and their relationship with the government.

Ever since ''The X-Files: I Want to Believe'' debuted in theaters, there was talk of a third ''X-Files'' movie to wrap-up the series' remaining storylines. However, for years these talks never resulted in action until on March 24, 2015, Fox announced that the series would return as a short-format event series with six episodes. After the season aired, it received mixed reviews from critics. The second, third, and fourth episodes were met with mostly positive comments, with "[[Mulder and Scully Meet the Were-Monster]]" receiving overwhelmingly positive comments. Conversely, the first, fifth, and sixth episodes were largely derided by critics. The [[Mythology of The X-Files|mythology episodes]], in particular, were poorly received.

==Plot overview==
Fourteen years after [[The Truth (The X-Files)|the closure of the X-Files]], [[Fox Mulder]] is contacted by [[Dana Scully]] at the behest of [[Federal Bureau of Investigation|FBI]] Assistant Director [[Walter Skinner]], who wants him to meet a right-wing online webcaster named Tad O'Malley. Mulder and Scully reunite in [[Washington, D.C.]], where they are picked up by O'Malley in his limousine. They meet a young woman named Sveta, who claims to have fragmented memories of having her [[fetus]]es stolen from her during [[alien abduction]]s and to possess alien DNA. 

O'Malley takes Mulder to a secret location where a [[Aurora (aircraft)|triangular aircraft]] (referred to as an "ARV", or Alien Replica Vehicle) built from alien technology is being housed. Mulder now believes that [[Colonist (The X-Files)|Colonization]] and the alien invasion were all an elaborate hoax to distract. Instead, Mulder thinks it was a "conspiracy of men" who have used extraterrestrial technology on human parties for decades, and these events were subsequently made to look like alien abductions. Before O'Malley can go public with his claims, his website is shut down, the "ARV" craft and its scientists are destroyed by heavily armed men dressed in military uniforms, and a [[UFO]] intercepts Sveta while she is driving, destroying her car. 

Scully reveals that Sveta's re-tested DNA sample confirms that she does in fact possess extraterrestrial DNA; a test Scully has performed on herself has revealed that she does as well. Mulder states that Sveta is the key to exposing the conspiracy and those responsible. They then receive an urgent summons from Skinner requesting them to meet him. The [[Cigarette Smoking Man]], now alive in the present day, receives word via telephone that the X-Files have been re-opened.<ref>{{cite episode |title=My Struggle |series=The X-Files |series-link=The X-Files |credits=[[Chris Carter (screenwriter)|Chris Carter]] (director); [[Chris Carter (screenwriter)|Chris Carter]] (writer) |network=[[Fox Broadcasting Company|Fox]] |season=10 |number=1}}</ref>

Six weeks after the events of "[[My Struggle (The X-Files)|My Struggle]]", Scully arrives at FBI headquarters to find that Mulder has disappeared after watching an excerpt from Tad O'Malley's online news broadcast. As Scully informs Skinner and Agent Liz Einstein of Mulder's absence, Mulder attempts to leave Washington—visibly unwell and badly bruised. O'Malley explains to Scully that he suspects that alien DNA has been injected into every American citizen in order to facilitate the widespread outbreak of the Spartan Virus. Designed to strip humans of their immune systems, this contagion quickly manifests itself nationwide, with Scully and Einstein noting a sharp increase in the number of patients admitted to hospitals and triage centers. 

Agent Kyd Miller finds a phone-tracking app on Mulder's computer and notes his position in [[Spartanburg, South Carolina]]. Scully receives a phone-call from former X-Files agent [[Monica Reyes]] to meet with her. Reyes reveals that Cigarette Smoking Man offered to secure both Scully and Reyes a place among the designated survivors of the end-times. Scully and Einstein attempt to develop a vaccine using Scully's DNA. Scully realizes that she is being protected from the contagion by a combination of the alien genomes that remained after she was abducted and experimented on, and the DNA anomalies instilled within her at the request of Reyes. 

Mulder approaches Cigarette Smoking Man, who offers him a chance to survive the outbreak. Mulder declines, and is found by Miller, who returns him to Washington with the hope of finding a cure. Scully travels to Mulder and Miller's location, finding them at the [[14th Street Bridges|14th Street Bridge]]. Miller asks how Mulder will survive, Scully replies that [[Baby William|William]], their son, will have to be the donor of a stem cell transplant. Mulder begins to succumb to the virus. Suddenly, a beam of light shines down onto Miller, Scully, and Mulder, and a triangle-shaped UFO slowly descends and hovers above them. The episode ends with Scully looking at the lights of the spacecraft, shining down directly onto her and her partners.<ref>{{cite episode |title=My Struggle II |series=The X-Files |series-link=The X-Files |credits=[[Chris Carter (screenwriter)|Chris Carter]] (director); [[Chris Carter (screenwriter)|Chris Carter]], [[Anne Simon]], and Margaret Fearon (writers) |network=[[Fox Broadcasting Company|Fox]] |season=10 |number=6}}</ref>

== Cast ==

=== Main cast===
* [[David Duchovny]] as [[Fox Mulder]], an FBI special agent assigned to the newly reopened X-Files division. He remains a believer in the paranormal and the existence of extraterrestrial life, though, throughout the season, his faith begins to waver. 
* [[Gillian Anderson]] as [[Dana Scully]], a medical doctor and FBI special agent assigned to the X-Files. Although an initial skeptic, after Mulder's abduction, she became more open-minded about the possibility of extraterrestrial life. 
* [[Mitch Pileggi]] as [[Walter Skinner]], an assistant director at the FBI and an ally of Mulder and Scully.{{efn|Only credited for the episodes he appears in.}}
{{notelist}}

=== Recurring cast ===
* [[William B. Davis]] as [[Cigarette Smoking Man]], a former government official, and nemesis of Mulder and Scully, who worked to cover up the truth of the existence of aliens and their plan to colonize the Earth.

=== Guest cast ===
* [[Joel McHale]] as Tad O'Malley, an Internet news anchor who is an ally of Mulder.
* [[Lauren Ambrose]] as Agent Liz Einstein, a medical doctor, Miller's partner, and a hard-skeptic.
* [[Robbie Amell]] as Agent Kyd Miller, an open-minded FBI agent who believes in the paranormal, and is Einstein's partner.
* [[Aliza Vellani]] as Sandeep, a nurse at the Our Lady of Sorrows Hospital. She acts as an assistant to [[Dana Scully]].
* [[Annabeth Gish]] as [[Monica Reyes]], an FBI special agent and ally to Mulder and Scully who was formerly assigned to the X-Files division.
* [[Bruce Harwood]] as [[The Lone Gunmen#John Fitzgerald Byers|John Fitzgerald Byers]], a member of [[The Lone Gunmen]].
* [[Tom Braidwood]] as [[The Lone Gunmen#Melvin Frohike|Melvin Frohike]], a member of The Lone Gunmen.
* [[Dean Haglund]] as [[The Lone Gunmen#Richard Langly|Richard Langly]], a member of The Lone Gunmen.
* [[Sheila Larken]] as [[List of minor The X-Files characters#Margaret Scully|Margaret Scully]], Scully's mother.
* [[Annet Mahendru]] as Sveta, a victim of multiple alien abductions.
* [[Rhys Darby]] as Guy Mann, a [[Shapeshifting|shape-shifter]].
* [[Kumail Nanjiani]] as Pasha, an animal control officer.

==Background==
''[[The X-Files]]'' aired from 1993 to 2002 on [[Fox Broadcasting Company|Fox]] and followed the efforts of federal agents [[Fox Mulder]] ([[David Duchovny]]) and [[Dana Scully]] ([[Gillian Anderson]]) as they investigated crimes linked to the paranormal. Following the series' seventh season, Duchovny scaled back his involvement substantially, appearing in only half of the eighth season's episodes, and only starring in two of season nine's.<ref name=space>{{cite web |author=Elber, Lynn |url=http://www.space.com/sciencefiction/tv/xfiles_duchovny_000518_wg.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20040924004848/http://space.com/sciencefiction/tv/xfiles_duchovny_000518_wg.html |archive-date=September 24, 2004 |title=Fox Mulder 'Ready to Get Back to Work' |website=[[Space.com]] |agency=Associated Press / Space |date=May 18, 2000 |access-date=July 5, 2009}}</ref><ref name="truthtruth">{{cite AV media |people=[[Chris Carter (screenwriter)|Carter, Chris]] |year=2002 |section=The Truth Behind Season 9: "The Truth" |medium=DVD |title=[[The X-Files season 9|The X-Files: The Complete Ninth Season]] |publisher=[[20th Century Fox Home Entertainment]]|display-authors=etal}}</ref> Likewise, during the ninth season, both Anderson and Carter had signed on at the last minute, with their contract extensions only lasting until the end of 2002, and Anderson specifically stated that she would leave the show following the conclusion of the season.<ref name=scifistaff>{{cite news |last1=''ScFiWire'' staff |title=The X-Files |website=ScFiWire |date=November 21, 2001}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=''The Hollywood Reporter'' staff |title=TV Talk |work=[[The Hollywood Reporter]] |date=October 15, 2001}}</ref><ref>Spelling, Ian. (February 2002) "Doggett's Pursuit". ''[[The X-Files merchandise|The X-Files Magazine]]''. Retrieved on October 1, 2009.</ref> During these final two seasons, FBI agents [[John Doggett]] ([[Robert Patrick]]) and [[Monica Reyes]] ([[Annabeth Gish]]) became the series' new leads.<ref name=doggettjohn>{{cite web |first1=Michael |last1=Fleming |first2=Josef |last2=Adalian |url=https://variety.com/2000/tv/news/patrick-marks-x-files-spot-1117784003/ |title=Patrick Marks 'X-Files' Spot |work=Variety |date=July 20, 2000 |access-date=November 27, 2009}}</ref><ref>{{cite video |people=[[Frank Spotnitz]], [[Robert Patrick]] |date=2002 |section=Profiles: Monica Reyes |title=[[The X-Files season 9|The X-Files: The Complete Ninth Season]] |medium=DVD |publisher=[[20th Century Fox Home Entertainment|Fox Home Entertainment]]}}</ref> Executive producer Frank Spotnitz speculated that the show could extend into a tenth and possibly eleventh season, if the show was able to attract an audience.<ref name=scifistaff/> However, the show lost viewers and was eventually cancelled by Fox.<ref name="TheTruthBehindSeasonNine">{{Cite AV media |people=[[Chris Carter (screenwriter)|Carter, Chris]] |year=2002 |section=The Truth Behind Season 9 |medium=DVD |title=[[The X-Files season 9|The X-Files: The Complete Ninth Season]] |publisher=[[Fox Broadcasting Company|Fox Home Entertainment]]|display-authors=etal}}</ref>

In 2008, both Duchovny and Anderson reprised their roles as Mulder and Scully in the film ''[[The X-Files: I Want to Believe]]''. In several interviews around the release, series creator [[Chris Carter (screenwriter)|Chris Carter]] said that if ''The X-Files: I Want to Believe'' proved successful at the box office, a third installment would be made going back to the TV series' mythology, focusing specifically on the alien invasion and colonization of Earth foretold in the series finale, due to occur on [[2012 phenomenon|December 22, 2012]].<ref name=thirdbelieve>{{cite news |url=http://insidemovies.ew.com/2008/04/18/chris-carter-wa/ |title='X-Files' Creator Chris Carter Wants to Believe in a Third Movie Featuring Mulder and Scully |author=Clark Collis |newspaper=[[Entertainment Weekly]] |publisher=[[Time Inc.|Time Inc]] |date=April 18, 2008 |access-date=July 27, 2009 |archive-date=May 3, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120503101833/http://insidemovies.ew.com/2008/04/18/chris-carter-wa/ |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=http://movies.ign.com/articles/895/895378p1.html |title=Carter Already Planning ''X-Files 3'' |author=Parfitt, Orlando |publisher=[[News Corporation (1980–2013)|News Corporation]] |work=[[IGN]] |date=July 31, 2008 |access-date=October 14, 2009}}</ref> In an October 2009 interview, Duchovny said he would want to do a 2012 ''X-Files'' film, but did not know if he would get the chance.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://movies.ign.com/articles/103/1035816p1.html |title=Duchovny on ''X-Files 3'' |author=Vejvoda, Jim |publisher=[[News Corporation (1980–2013)|News Corporation]] |work=[[IGN]] |date=October 16, 2009 |access-date=October 19, 2009}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.news.com.au/entertainment/movies/david-duchovny-talks-gay-crushes-and-a-possible-x-files-sequel/story-e6frfmvr-1225985310023 |title=David Duchovny Talks Gay Crushes and a Possible X-Files Sequel |newspaper=[[The Daily Telegraph]] |date=January 11, 2011 |access-date=January 11, 2011 |archive-date=October 27, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151027015032/http://www.news.com.au/entertainment/movies/david-duchovny-talks-gay-crushes-and-a-possible-x-files-sequel/story-e6frfmvr-1225985310023 |url-status=dead }}</ref> 

Anderson stated in August 2012 that a third ''X-Files'' film was "looking pretty good".<ref>{{cite news |last=Marcus |first=Stephanie |title=Gillian Anderson: 'X-Files 3' Movie Is 'Looking Pretty Good' |url=https://www.huffingtonpost.com/2012/08/27/gillian-anderson-x-files-3-movie_n_1833518.html |access-date=September 4, 2012 |newspaper=[[The Huffington Post]] |publisher=[[AOL]] |date=August 27, 2012}}</ref> At the October 2013 [[New York Comic Con]], Duchovny and Anderson reaffirmed that they and Carter are interested in making a third film, with Anderson saying "If it takes fan encouragement to get Fox interested in that, then I guess that's what it would be."<ref>{{cite news |title=David Duchovny, Gillian Anderson Want to Reunite for Third 'X-Files' Movie |url=http://www.nydailynews.com/entertainment/tv-movies/duchovny-anderson-reunite-3rd-x-files-movie-article-1.1484745 |access-date=October 14, 2013 |work=[[New York Daily News]] |publisher=Daily News, L.P. |agency=Associated Press |date=October 14, 2013}}</ref> In January  2015, [[Fox Television Stations|Fox Television Group]] chairman and CEO Gary Newman revealed that there was network interest in reviving ''The X-Files'', not as a film franchise, but as a six-episode limited run.<ref name=initialpostaboutrevival>{{cite web |last1=Porter |first1=Rick |title=Fox Wants to Believe 'The X-Files' Could Return Once More |url=http://www.zap2it.com/blogs/x-files_return_fox_gillian_anderson_david_duchovny-2015-01 |website=[[Zap2it]] |publisher=[[Tribune Digital Ventures]] |access-date=March 24, 2015 |date=January 17, 2015 |archive-date=June 30, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150630075315/http://www.zap2it.com/blogs/x-files_return_fox_gillian_anderson_david_duchovny-2015-01 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

==Broadcast==
The season had a two-night premiere on Fox, debuting on Sunday, January 24, 2016, with the following episode airing on Monday at 8:00 pm, the timeslot in which the remaining episodes also aired.<ref name="airingslot">{{cite web |last=Ausiello |first=Michael |title=Fox Fall Schedule: ''Scream Queens'' Takes Tuesday Crown, ''Sleepy'' Rises on Thursday, ''X-Files'' Held 'Til January |url=https://www.tvline.com/news/fox-fall-tv-schedule-scream-queens-tuesday-x-files-midseason-612005/ |work=TVLine |access-date=May 11, 2015 |date=May 11, 2015}}</ref> The premiere episode was screened at New York Comic Con on October 10, 2015.<ref>{{cite web |title=''The X-Files'' Revival Premiere to Screen at NY Comic-Con in October |url=http://tvline.com/2015/09/10/the-x-files-revival-premiere-ny-comic-con/ |work=TVLine |first=Michael |last=Slezak |date=September 10, 2015 |access-date=September 11, 2015 |archive-date=September 11, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150911190043/http://tvline.com/2015/09/10/the-x-files-revival-premiere-ny-comic-con/ |url-status=dead }}</ref>

Internationally, the season premiered in Canada on [[CTV Television Network|CTV]] on January 24, 2016, simultaneous with the American broadcast.<ref>{{cite web |title=Fox's 'The X-Files' Revival Acquired by CTV for Canada |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/foxs-x-files-revival-acquired-844768 |work=The Hollywood Reporter |first=Etan |last=Vlessing |date=December 1, 2015 |access-date=January 15, 2016}}</ref> It premiered in Ireland on [[RTÉ2]] on January 26, 2016, two days after its U.S. premiere.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.rte.ie/ten/news/2016/0107/758318-the-good-wife-returns-and-other-new-year-tv-news/ |title=Dramas to Watch on Irish TV in 2016 |publisher=RTÉ Ten |date=January 7, 2016 |access-date=January 18, 2016}}</ref> It premiered in Australia on [[Network Ten]] on January 31, 2016.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://tenplay.com.au/channel-ten/the-x-files/extra/season-2016/x-files-premiere-date-announced |title=The X-Files Premiere Date Announced |date=January 12, 2016 |publisher=Tenplay |access-date=January 15, 2016 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160120003846/http://tenplay.com.au/channel-ten/the-x-files/extra/season-2016/x-files-premiere-date-announced |archive-date=January 20, 2016 |df=mdy-all}}</ref> It premiered in the United Kingdom on [[Channel 5 (UK)|Channel 5]] on February 8, 2016, where it became the highest-rated drama in the channel's history.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.digitalspy.com/tv/the-x-files/news/a783816/the-x-files-becomes-channel-5s-highest-rating-drama-ever-in-final-figures/ |title=The X-Files Becomes Channel 5's Highest Rating Drama Ever in Final Figures |work=[[Digital Spy]] |date=February 17, 2016 |access-date=February 18, 2016}}</ref>

[[Fox International Channels]], where available, premiered the series the day after the American premiere.<ref>{{cite web |title=The X-Files Getting a Day & Date Release Across FOX International Channels Markets |url=http://foxinternationalchannels.com/press/the-x-files-getting-a-day-date-release-across-fox-international-channels-markets |publisher=[[Fox Broadcasting Company|Fox International]] |access-date=January 16, 2016 |date=December 17, 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Jaafar |first1=Ali |title=Fox International Releasing 'The X-Files' Day-And-Date In 60+ Countries |url=https://deadline.com/2015/12/fox-x-files-mulder-scully-day-date-60-countries-chris-carter-1201668750/ |work=[[Deadline Hollywood]] |access-date=January 16, 2016 |date=December 17, 2015}}</ref>

==Production==

===Casting===
[[File:Gillian Anderson & David Duchovny (9344570889).jpg|right|thumb|The revival features [[Gillian Anderson]] (''left'') and [[David Duchovny]] (''right''), pictured in 2013, reprising their roles as [[Dana Scully]] and [[Fox Mulder]], respectively.]]
Once Newman revealed thoughts of bringing back the series, he noted that the revival would include "all key players": Carter, Duchovny, and Anderson.<ref name=mirror1/> Fox TV Group chairman [[Dana Walden]] later noted that finding the ideal time that the three key members of the series were free would pose a challenge.<ref name=deadline.com/> At the time of the announcement, Duchovny was working on the [[NBC]] series ''[[Aquarius (U.S. TV series)|Aquarius]]'', and Anderson was involved in the [[BBC]] drama ''[[The Fall (TV series)|The Fall]]''.<ref name=cnn23>{{cite web |last1=France |first1=Lisa Respers |title=Is 'The X-Files' Coming Back? The Truth is Out There |url=http://www.cnn.com/2015/03/23/entertainment/x-files-series-return-feat/ |publisher=[[Time Warner]] |work=[[CNN]] |access-date=March 24, 2015 |date=March 23, 2015}}</ref> However, both co-stars expressed their desire to return to the series: prior to Newman's announcement, Anderson said that she would be "fucking overjoyed" if Fox brought back ''The X-Files'', and Duchovny said that he would be "more than happy" to reprise his role as Mulder.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nme.com/filmandtv/news/new-the-x-files-tv-series-with-david-duchovny-gill/367915 |title=New 'The X-Files' TV Series with David Duchovny, Gillian Anderson in the Works |publisher=[[Time Inc. UK]] |work=[[NME]] |date=January 19, 2015 |access-date=March 24, 2015}}</ref><ref name="usa today">{{cite news |last1=McClurg |first1=Jocelyn |title=David Duchovny is Onboard for 'X-Files' Reboot |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/life/tv/2015/01/20/david-duchovny-x-files-return-gillian-anderson/22063573/ |access-date=March 24, 2015 |work=[[USA Today]] |publisher=[[Gannett Company]] |date=January 20, 2015}}</ref> 

In a later interview with ''[[GQ]]'' magazine, Anderson revealed that, when asked about returning for a television continuation of the program, she was hesitant, since she assumed the network would want to order over twenty new episodes (the length of a season when the show had originally aired). When it was revealed that the network would only order a short run, she enthusiastically agreed to reprise her role.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Larson |first1=Lauren |title=Gillian Anderson Answers All Your Questions about the New X-Files Revival |url=https://www.gq.com/story/gillian-anderson-x-files-revival-quiz |website=[[GQ (magazine)|GQ]] |access-date=January 20, 2016 |date=January 19, 2016}}</ref> Initially, Anderson was offered half the pay of Duchovny, but she negotiated her contract so that both leads received the same amount.<ref>{{cite web |last1=O'Connell |first1=Michael |title=When 'The X-Files' Became A-List: An Oral History of Fox's Out-There Success Story |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/features/x-files-became-a-list-852398 |work=[[The Hollywood Reporter]] |access-date=January 22, 2016 |date=January 7, 2016}}</ref>

Early on, it was reported that an offer went out for [[Mitch Pileggi]], who played [[Walter Skinner]], to reprise his role, and that "other key cast members will also return."<ref name=tvwiseinitialreport/> [[William B. Davis]], the actor who portrayed [[Cigarette Smoking Man]], also noted that he was asked about his availability during the summer of 2015, hinting that his character would return in some form.<ref name=vancouvercitation1>{{cite web |last1=Grainger |first1=Peter |title=New 'X-Files' Episodes to Shoot in Vancouver, Smoking Man Confirms |url=https://www.ctvnews.ca/vancouver/article/new-x-files-episodes-to-shoot-in-vancouver-smoking-man-confirms/ |publisher=[[CIVT-DT|CTV Vancouver]] |access-date=March 27, 2015 |date=March 26, 2015}}</ref> Later, Duchovny revealed during his March 31, 2015, appearance on ''[[Late Show with David Letterman]]'' that both Pileggi and Davis would return for the season.<ref>{{cite magazine |url=https://www.ew.com/article/2015/03/31/x-files-skinner-smoking |title=''X-Files'' Revival Plans Return of Walter Skinner, Cigarette Smoking Man |magazine=[[Entertainment Weekly]] |publisher=[[Time Inc.|Time Inc]] |first=James |last=Hibberd |date=March 31, 2015 |access-date=April 1, 2015}}</ref> Pileggi confirmed his return in April 2015.<ref>{{cite magazine |url=https://www.ew.com/article/2015/04/20/mitch-pileggi-reprise-role-walter-skinner-x-files-revival |title=Mitch Pileggi to Reprise Role as Walter Skinner in ''X-Files'' Revival |publisher=[[Time Inc.|Time Inc]] |magazine=[[Entertainment Weekly]] |date=April 20, 2015 |access-date=April 21, 2015 |last=Connolly |first=Kelly}}</ref> 

In an interview with XFilesNews.com, Carter expressed hope in having [[Robert Patrick]] and [[Annabeth Gish]] reprise their roles as [[John Doggett]] and [[Monica Reyes]], respectively, although their involvement would be contingent upon their current acting commitments.<ref name=xfilesnews.com>{{cite web |last1=Quijada |first1=Avi |title=XFN Exclusive: Chris Carter on #XFilesRevival |url=http://www.xfiles.news/index.php/news/latest-news/85-xfn-exclusive-chris-carter-on-xfilesrevival |publisher=XFilesNews |access-date=March 29, 2015 |date=March 25, 2015 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160125142527/http://www.xfiles.news/index.php/news/latest-news/85-xfn-exclusive-chris-carter-on-xfilesrevival |archive-date=January 25, 2016 }}</ref> Patrick ruled out a return, but it was confirmed in August 2015 that Gish was returning for at least one episode.<ref name="Reyes">{{cite web |last1=Roots |first1=Kimberely |title=''The X-Files'': Annabeth Gish to Reprise Reyes in Fox's Revival |url=http://tvline.com/2015/08/11/xfiles-annabeth-gish-revival-cast-agent-reyes/ |work=[[TVLine]] |access-date=August 12, 2015 |date=August 11, 2015 |archive-date=August 12, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150812184030/http://tvline.com/2015/08/11/xfiles-annabeth-gish-revival-cast-agent-reyes/ |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.denofgeek.us/tv/the-x-files/243258/the-x-files-revival-news-robert-patrick-says-no-agent-doggett |title=The X-Files Revival News: Robert Patrick Says No Agent Doggett |publisher=Den of Geek |first=Chris |last=Longo |date=May 1, 2015 |access-date=May 3, 2015}}</ref> [[Laurie Holden]] did not rule out a return as [[Marita Covarrubias]],<ref>{{cite web |last1=Burlingam |first1=Russ |title=The Walking Dead's Laurie Holden Doesn't Rule Out Possible X-Files Return |url=https://comicbook.com/2015/04/06/the-walking-deads-laurie-holden-doesnt-rule-out-possible-x-files/ |publisher=ComicBook.com |access-date=April 6, 2015 |date=April 6, 2015}}</ref> but did not appear in any of the episodes. [[Joel McHale]] was announced as a guest star in June 2015, playing Tad O'Malley, an Internet news anchor who is an ally of Mulder's.<ref name=joelmchalecasting>{{cite web |url=http://tvline.com/2015/06/03/x-files-joel-mchale-revival-cast/ |title=''X-Files'' Revival Casts Joel McHale as Mulder's Dubious Ally |website=TVLine |first=Kimberly |last=Roots |date=June 3, 2015 |access-date=June 3, 2015 |archive-date=February 22, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160222104010/http://tvline.com/2015/06/03/x-files-joel-mchale-revival-cast/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> Carter chose to cast McHale after his [[Roast (comedy)|roast]] of [[Barack Obama]] at the 2014 [[White House Correspondents' Association#White House Correspondents' dinner|White House Correspondents' Dinner]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/news/reliable-source/wp/2016/01/19/excited-about-joel-mchales-role-in-the-x-files-reboot-thank-the-white-house-correspondents-dinner/ |title=Excited About Joel McHale's Role in the X-Files Reboot? Thank the White House Correspondents' Dinner |newspaper=[[The Washington Post]] |date=January 19, 2016 |access-date=January 20, 2016 |first1=Emily |last1=Heil}}</ref>

===Writing===
{{Quote box
 | quote = We're going to tell X-Files the way that we've always told them; we will of course set them in the time and place that they exist. We're telling contemporary stories about contemporary situations, true to Mulder and Scully's characters and their relationship and the passage of time.
 | source = —[[Chris Carter (screenwriter)|Chris Carter]], on the nature of ''The X-Files'' revival.<ref name=xfilesnews.com/>
 | width  = 30em
 | bgcolor= #CCCCFF
 | align  = right
 | quoted = 1
}}
Carter himself was also confirmed to be helming the project, serving as writer and executive producer.<ref name=tvwiseinitialreport/> Carter later confirmed that [[Darin Morgan]] and [[James Wong (filmmaker)|James Wong]] would return to the series as writers, and [[Glen Morgan]] would return in a "productorial position".<ref name=xfilesnews.com/> Wong and Glen Morgan had served as writers for the series during its first, second, and fourth seasons,<ref name="DVDseason1">{{cite AV media notes |title=The X-Files: The Complete First Season |title-link=The X-Files season 1 |others=[[Robert Mandel]], et al. |type=booklet |publisher=[[Fox Broadcasting Corporation]]}}</ref><ref name="DVDseason2">{{cite AV media notes |title=The X-Files: The Complete Second Season |title-link=The X-Files season 2 |others=[[David Nutter]], et al. |type=booklet |publisher=[[Fox Broadcasting Corporation]]}}</ref><ref name="DVD">{{cite AV media notes |title=The X-Files: The Complete Fourth Season |title-link=The X-Files season 4 |others=[[R. W. Goodwin]], et al. |type=booklet |publisher=[[Fox Broadcasting Corporation]]}}</ref> and Darin Morgan had provided several scripts for the series during its second and third seasons.<ref name="DVDseason2"/><ref name="DVDseason3">{{cite AV media notes |title=The X-Files: The Complete Third Season |title-link=The X-Files season 3 |others=[[R. W. Goodwin]], et al. |type=booklet |publisher=[[Fox Broadcasting Corporation]]}}</ref> Following the announcement of the season, it was speculated as to whether long-time Carter collaborator [[Frank Spotnitz]] would return to assist with the writing, although this did not come to pass.<ref name=tvwiseinitialreport/> In addition, former ''X-Files'' writer [[Vince Gilligan]] noted that he would have enjoyed returning to the series, but his busy work schedule did not allow it; he later said, "I'll be watching every episode and rooting them on".<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.denofgeek.us/tv/the-x-files/243988/vince-gilligan-would-love-to-be-involved-with-x-files-revival |title=Vince Gilligan Would 'Love' To Be Involved With X-Files Revival |work=Den of Geek |date=February 23, 2015 |access-date=March 24, 2015}}</ref><ref name="newinfo">{{cite web |last1=Mangla |first1=Ismat |title='The X-Files' Revival Update: Filming Starts June 8, Celebrated Writers To Return |url=http://www.ibtimes.com/x-files-revival-update-filming-starts-june-8-celebrated-writers-return-1905849 |website=[[International Business Times]] |publisher=[[IBT Media]] |access-date=May 2, 2015 |date=May 2, 2015}}</ref>

[[Mark Snow]] also reprised his role as the series' composer.<ref name=xfilesnews.com/> "There are some new musical elements I've brought in for certain moments in the episodes," said Snow. "It's difficult to describe what is so completely different about them, except that there are some different sounds, different pulsing percussion elements, and different ambient designs, but the basic harmonic structure from the past is fairly intact."<ref>{{cite web |url=http://musiquefantastique.com/mark-snow-the-return-of-the-x-files/ |title=Interview with Mark Snow: Scoring the X-Files Mini-Series |publisher=Musique Fantastique |date=January 23, 2016 |access-date=January 25, 2016 |last=Larson |first=Randall D. |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160128024343/http://musiquefantastique.com/mark-snow-the-return-of-the-x-files/ |archive-date=January 28, 2016 |df=mdy-all}}</ref>

Prior to filming, Carter explained that he had "ideas for every [character]" and that the season would strive to tell fresh stories in a "very new political environment".<ref name=xfilesnews.com/> He explained that, since the original conclusion of the series back in 2002, he had been collecting noteworthy news stories for future use. Carter revealed that the seasons' plot has no connection to the [[The X-Files Season 10 (comics)|''Season 10'' comic book series]], and is composed of both [[Mythology of The X-Files|mythology episodes]], as well as stand-alone "[[Villain of the week|Monster-of-the-Week]]" episodes.<ref name=xfilesnews.com/> It was later confirmed by Carter that the first and sixth episodes would be mythology episodes, and others would be standalones.<ref name="mythology">{{cite web |url=https://ign.com/articles/2015/10/10/nycc-2015-the-x-files-revival-season-is-half-mythology-half-standalone-episodes |title=NYCC 2015: The X-Files Revival Season Is Half Mythology, Half Standalone Episodes |website=IGN |first1=Terri |last1=Schwartz |first2=Scott |last2=Collura |date=October 10, 2015 |access-date=October 11, 2015}}</ref> Carter wrote the teleplays and directed the first, fifth, and sixth episodes.<ref name=newinfo/><ref name=mystruggle>{{cite web |title=What Do We Know From a Callsheet? |url=http://www.xfiles.news/index.php/news/latest-news/646-spoiler-what-do-we-know-from-a-callsheet |publisher=XFilesNews |access-date=June 17, 2015 |date=June 17, 2015}}</ref><ref name="ChrisEpisode4">{{cite tweet |author=Anne Simon|author-link=Anne Simon |user=Annealiz1 |title=Tagging along with Chris Carter tomorrow on location with #XFiles episode 4, written/directed by Chris. Hoping for good pics and live tweets |number=628051374790410240 |access-date=August 3, 2015 |date=August 3, 2015}}</ref><ref name=finalecredit>{{cite tweet |author=Anne Simon|author-link=Anne Simon |user=Annealiz1 |number=630723977816707072 |title=Chris has confirmed. Will get story credit on #XFiles episode 6 with BFF Margaret Fearon who gave medical advice and is real live Scully. |date=August 10, 2015 |access-date=August 10, 2015}}</ref> 

The second, "Founder's Mutation", was written and directed by James Wong. The third, "[[Mulder and Scully Meet the Were-Monster]]", was written and directed by Darin Morgan. The fourth episode, titled "Home Again", was written and directed by Glen Morgan.<ref name="GlenMorganEp2">{{cite web |url=http://tvline.com/2015/06/04/the-x-files-home-again-season-10-episode-2-glen-morgan/ |title=''X-Files'' Revival on Fox: Are We Getting a Sequel to the Season 4 Classic 'Home'? |work=TVLine |first=Michael |last=Ausiello |date=June 4, 2015 |access-date=June 4, 2015 |archive-date=August 7, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150807182242/http://tvline.com/2015/06/04/the-x-files-home-again-season-10-episode-2-glen-morgan/ |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref name="weremonstername">{{cite web |url=https://www.tvline.com/news/supernatural-season-11-spoilers-cast-amara-femme-fatale-621779/ |title=Ask Ausiello: Spoilers on ''CSI'' Finale, ''Arrow'', ''Supernatural'', ''X-Files'', ''Hannibal'', ''Secrets & Lies'' and More! |work=TVLine |date=June 24, 2015 |access-date=June 24, 2015 |last=Ausiello |first=Michael}}</ref><ref name="JamesWong">{{cite tweet |author=X-Files News |user=XFilesNews |number=628335218764718080 |title=Episode No. 5 of #XFilesRevival is going to be written and directed by #JamesWong @thexfiles #thexfiles |date=August 3, 2015 |access-date=August 4, 2015}}</ref> Scientist and biology professor [[Anne Simon]], who first consulted on the series' first-season finale episode "[[The Erlenmeyer Flask]]", and for the rest of the original series run, returned as a biology science advisor.<ref name="wtop">{{cite web |url=http://wtop.com/tv/2015/07/umd-professor-provides-science-behind-x-files/ |title=U.Md. Professor Provides the Science Behind 'The X-Files' |publisher=WTOP/Washington's Top News |date=July 30, 2015 |access-date=August 2, 2015 |last=Forzato |first=Jamie |quote=Anne Simon, a plant virologist at the University of Maryland, has been the science adviser for "The X-Files" almost since the beginning. She's excited about the revival, which she's also worked on.}}</ref> She later received writing credit for her contributions to the finale.<ref name=finalecredit/> A seventh episode, based on a spec script, was written. It was not produced due to scheduling conflicts. According to Carter, if Fox orders more episodes, this unfilmed episode will be made.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.tvline.com/news/the-x-files-revival-episode-7-fox-625911/ |title=''X-Files'' Revival: An Extra Hour Is Out There — Scoop on Ill-Fated Episode 7 |work=TVLine |first=Michael |last=Ausiello |date=October 12, 2015 |access-date=October 12, 2015}}</ref>

===Filming===
In March 2015, it was claimed by several sources that the network would order a short-run season of fewer than ten episodes, with an initial guess of six. The decision to cut the order down to only a few installments was reportedly done so that the network could work around the busy schedules of Duchovny and Anderson. Duchovny said he had no interest in doing a full season because: "We're all old, we don't have the energy for a full season."<ref name="usa today"/><ref name=tvwiseinitialreport/><ref>{{cite web |last1=Longo |first1=Chris |title=The X-Files Reboot News: Season Order Details, Returning Cast, and More |url=http://www.denofgeek.us/tv/the-x-files/243258/the-x-files-reboot-news-season-order-details-returning-cast-and-more |archive-url=https://archive.today/20150404131108/http://www.denofgeek.us/tv/the-x-files/243258/the-x-files-reboot-news-season-order-details-returning-cast-and-more |url-status=dead |archive-date=April 4, 2015 |publisher=Den of Geek |access-date=March 24, 2015 |date=March 23, 2015 }}</ref> The article claimed that, if all went as planned, the season would begin filming in the summer of 2015.<ref name=tvwiseinitialreport>{{cite web |last1=Munn |first1=Patrick |title='The X-Files' Revival Nears Greenlight At Fox; Network Eyes Short Order, Gillian Anderson & David Duchovny To Return |url=http://www.tvwise.co.uk/2015/03/the-x-files-revival-nears-greenlight-at-fox-network-eyes-short-order-gillian-anderson-david-duchovny-to-return/ |website=tvwise.co.uk |access-date=March 24, 2015 |date=March 20, 2015}}</ref><ref name=ign23>{{cite web |last1=Watts |first1=Steve |title=Rumor: X-Files Revival Deal Close; Could Shoot This Summer |url=https://www.ign.com/articles/2015/03/23/rumor-x-files-revival-deal-close-could-shoot-this-summer |website=[[IGN]] |publisher=[[j2 Global]] |access-date=March 24, 2015 |date=March 23, 2015}}</ref> It was confirmed by both Davis and Carter that the series would return to [[Vancouver]] for filming.<ref name=vancouvercitation1/><ref name=xfilesnews.com/> Filming began on June 8 and finished on September 3.<ref name=newinfo/><ref>{{cite tweet |author=Production Weekly |user=prodweek |title=Updated production schedule for @thexfilesfox is now… June 8 - August 22 #XFiles |number=597878563451183104 |access-date=May 25, 2015 |date=May 11, 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.huffingtonpost.ca/2015/06/10/xfiles-filming-vancouver-photos_n_7554254.html |title='X-Files' Filming Begins In Vancouver |work=The Huffington Post |first=Jesse |last=Ferreras |date=June 10, 2015 |access-date=June 11, 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite tweet |author=Gillian Anderson|author-link=Gillian Anderson |user=GillianA |number=639446834746777600 |title=That's a wrap on #XFiles Season 10! See you on January 24th! @davidduchovny @RobbieAmell @thexfiles |date=September 3, 2015 |access-date=September 4, 2015}}</ref>

== Reception ==

=== Reviews ===
Critical reception to this season has been mixed. The first and last episodes were met with lukewarm to negative reviews from critics, whereas episodes two through five were generally well received.<ref name="rottentomatoes" /> Overall, the [[review aggregator]] [[Metacritic]] gave it a score of 60 out of 100 based on 35 reviews, indicating "mixed or average" reviews.<ref>{{cite web |title=The X-Files: Season 10 |url=https://www.metacritic.com/tv/the-x-files/season-10 |website=[[Metacritic]] |access-date=January 23, 2016}}</ref> Likewise, [[Rotten Tomatoes]] gave the revival a 64% approval rating with an average score of 6.5 out of 10 based on 180 reviews. The site's consensus reads, "Gillian Anderson and David Duchovny's chemistry remains intact, but overall, ''The X-Files'' revival lacks the creative spark necessary to sustain the initial rush of nostalgia."<ref name="rottentomatoes">{{cite web |title=The X-Files: Season 10 |url=https://www.rottentomatoes.com/tv/the-x-files/s10/ |website=[[Rotten Tomatoes]] |access-date=January 23, 2016}}</ref>

[[My Struggle (The X-Files)|"My Struggle"]] debuted to a select crowd at the 2015 [[New York Comic Con]], and critical reception was mostly positive. Sadie Gennis of ''[[TV Guide]]'' wrote, "The episode immediately establishes that this is not a reboot nor a mere cash grab, but a thoughtful continuation of the beloved franchise."<ref>{{cite web |last1=Gennis |first1=Sadie |title=''The X-Files'' Premiere Will Make You a Believer |url=https://www.tvguide.com/news/the-x-files-season-10-premiere-review/ |website=[[TV Guide]] |access-date=January 15, 2016 |date=October 10, 2015}}</ref>  Chris Eggerstein of [[HitFix]] wrote that the tone of the revival was very reminiscent of the show's original run, and that "if you were a fan of the old ''X-Files'', you're probably going to like the new ''X-Files'' just fine."<ref>{{cite web |last1=Eggerstein |first1=Chris |title=First 'X-Files' Episode Reaction: Modern-Day Paranoia Wrapped in Comforting Nostalgia |url=http://www.hitfix.com/news/first-x-files-episode-reaction-modern-day-paranoia-wrapped-in-comforting-nostalgia |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151105062455/http://www.hitfix.com/news/first-x-files-episode-reaction-modern-day-paranoia-wrapped-in-comforting-nostalgia |url-status=dead |archive-date=November 5, 2015 |website=[[HitFix]] |access-date=January 15, 2016 |date=October 30, 2015}}</ref> Jane Mulkerrins of ''[[The Daily Telegraph|The Telegraph]]'' called the debut "fresh" and "one of the highlights" of the convention. Furthermore, she noted that the premiere was popular with fans, who greeted the episode with a standing ovation.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/culture/tvandradio/tv-and-radio-reviews/11922976/The-X-Files-first-look-review-A-fresh-take-on-this-classic-really-is-out-there.html |title=The X-Files, First Look Review: A Fresh Take on this Classic Really is Out There |work=[[The Daily Telegraph|The Telegraph]] |date=October 10, 2015 |access-date=January 15, 2016 |first1=Jane |last1=Mulkerrins}}</ref>

Pre-release reviews of "My Struggle" released after the New York Comic Con were more critical, with the consensus of many reviewers being that the first episode was not good.<ref name=digg>{{cite web |last1=Fallon |first1=Dan |title=What Do Critics Have To Say About The New 'X-Files' Season? |url=http://digg.com/2016/x-files-reviews-anderson-duchovny-revival-fox |publisher=[[Digg]] |access-date=January 21, 2016 |date=January 21, 2016}}</ref> Reviewing the premiere episode, Brian Lowry of ''[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]'' panned the revival of the series, "It's simply hard to escape the prevailing malaise of this being a deal-driven exercise, a chance to cash in on the name recognition of the title in a format that mitigated the time commitment for all concerned."<ref>{{cite web |url=https://variety.com/2016/tv/reviews/x-files-review-revival-david-duchovny-gillian-anderson-1201675982/ |title=TV Review: 'The X-Files' |first=Brian |last=Lowry |work=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]] |date=January 12, 2016 |access-date=January 13, 2016}}</ref> Similarly, Tim Goodman, writing for ''[[The Hollywood Reporter]]'', described the premiere as "a very underwhelming hour that will force even diehard fans [...] to consider whether pushing onward is really worth the time.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/review/x-files-tv-review-854844 |title='The X-Files': TV Review |work=[[The Hollywood Reporter]] |access-date=January 12, 2016 |first=Tim |last=Goodman |date=January 12, 2016}}</ref> 

Matt Fowler of [[IGN]] awarded it a 7.2 out of 10, denoting a "good" episode. Fowler wrote positively of Sveta's performance, and he also applauded the focus on the conspiracy as well as the episode's ending. However, he criticized it for having a "bored, disinterested tone".<ref>{{cite web |last1=Fowler |first1=Matt |title=The X-Files: "My Struggle" Review |url=https://www.ign.com/articles/2016/01/14/the-x-files-my-struggle-review |work=[[IGN]] |access-date=January 15, 2016 |date=January 13, 2016}}</ref> Alex McCown of ''[[The A.V. Club]]'' reviewed the first three episodes of the revival and awarded them collectively a "B+". He largely derided the first episode, writing that "it indulges in all of [Chris Carter's] worst [writing] tendencies."<ref name="avclubcombo"/> He was particularly critical of the episodes's expository monologues. Ultimately, he wrote that "the first episode demonstrates some of ''The X-Files''' weaker tendencies, though it possesses a hokey charm, one that comes from pretending as though the past 15 years of television never happened."<ref name="avclubcombo"/>

Pre-release reviews of the following two episodes were much more positive. McCown argued that it "immediately course corrects" with Wong's "Founder's Mutation"; he called the episode "smart" and "unsettling".<ref name="avclubcombo"/> McCown lauded Morgan's "Mulder and Scully Meet the Were-Monster", writing that the episode ultimately "makes the case for why ''The X-Files'' is still worth having around."<ref name="avclubcombo">{{cite web |url=https://www.avclub.com/review/meet-new-x-files-same-old-x-files-230759 |title=Meet the New ''X-Files'', Same as the Old ''X-Files'' |publisher=[[The Onion]] |work=[[The A.V. Club]] |date=January 18, 2016 |access-date=January 18, 2016 |author=McCown, Alex}}</ref> Brian Tallerico of [[Roger Ebert|RogerEbert.com]] wrote that "Founder's Mutation" "perfectly blends show mythology (including Mulder and Scully's kid) with a modern plot" and that "Mulder and Scully Meet the Were-Monster" is "hysterical, smart and so much fun".<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.rogerebert.com/demanders/return-of-the-x-files-stumbles-but-quickly-recovers |title=Return of ''The X-Files'' Stumbles But Quickly Recovers |publisher=[[Roger Ebert|RogerEbert.com]] |date=January 2, 2016 |access-date=January 21, 2016 |author=Tallerico, Brian}}</ref> Darren Franich of ''[[Entertainment Weekly]]'' reiterated these thoughts, arguing that "Founder's Mutation" is "an improvement over the premiere", and that Darin Morgan's episode is "a wild, playful, brain-twisting, heart-pulling, and above all adventurous episode of television."<ref>{{cite magazine |url=https://www.ew.com/article/2016/01/19/x-files-ew-review |title=''The X-Files'' EW Review: Never Better, Never Worse |magazine=[[Entertainment Weekly]] |date=January 19, 2016 |access-date=January 21, 2016 |author=Franich, Darren}}</ref>

===Ratings===

Before the season even began filming, an anonymous network insider revealed that Fox was interested in reviving the series because it would be a ratings success, noting: "The network feels that they can draw huge numbers and a PR drive to bring back a show which offers both drama and a built-in cult following."<ref name="mirror1">{{cite news |url=https://www.mirror.co.uk/tv/tv-news/x-files-coming-back-mulder-5000711?ICID=FB_mirror_main |title=The X Files is Coming Back as Mulder and Scully Ask Again if the Truth is Out There |publisher=[[Trinity Mirror]] |date=January 18, 2015 |access-date=March 24, 2015 |first1=Mark |last1=Jefferies |newspaper=[[Daily Mirror|Mirror.co.uk]]}}</ref> It was speculated that the success of the ''[[24: Live Another Day]]'' event series, which aired in 2014, inspired Fox to revive ''The X-Files''.<ref name=deadline.com>{{cite web |last1=Andreeva |first1=Nellie |title=Fox Confirms 'X-Files' Reboot Talks, David Duchovny & Gillian Anderson To Return – Update |url=https://deadline.com/2015/01/x-files-reboot-talks-fox-1201352465/ |publisher=[[Penske Media Corporation]] |work=[[Deadline Hollywood]] |access-date=March 24, 2015 |date=January 17, 2015}}</ref>

"My Struggle" debuted on January 24, 2016, and was watched by 16.19 million viewers. It scored a 6.1 [[Nielsen rating]] in the 18- to 49-year-old demographic. Nielsen ratings are [[audience measurement]] systems that determine the audience size and composition of [[broadcast programming|television programming]] in the United States, which means that 6.1 percent of all individuals aged 18- to 49-years old were watching at the time of the episode's airing.<ref name=minipremratings/> In terms of viewers, this made "My Struggle" the highest-rated premiere, since the [[The X-Files season 7|seventh season]] opener "[[The Sixth Extinction (The X-Files)|The Sixth Extinction]]" in 1999, which was viewed by 17.82 million people.<ref name="7comp">Shapiro (2000), p. 281</ref> It was the most-watched episode of ''The X-Files'' to air since the [[The X-Files season 8|eighth season]] episode "[[This Is Not Happening (The X-Files)|This Is Not Happening]]" in 2001, which was watched by 16.9 million viewers.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://iw.newsbank.com/resources/doc/nb/news/0EFD5CCC6E6B273B?p=NewsBank |title=Blame it on Cable |publisher=[[Advance Publications]] |date=March 1, 2001 |access-date=September 19, 2012 |last=Sepinwall |first=Alan |author2=Seitz, Matt Zoller |newspaper=[[The Star-Ledger]]}}</ref> When [[Digital video recorder|DVR]] and [[Streaming media|streaming]] are taken into account, "My Struggle" was seen by 21.4 million viewers, scoring a 7.1 Nielsen rating.<ref name=biggerratings>{{cite magazine |last1=Hibberd |first1=James |title=X-Files Return Ratings Grow to Top its own Series Finale |url=https://www.ew.com/article/2016/01/29/x-files-ratings |magazine=[[Entertainment Weekly]] |date=January 29, 2016 |access-date=January 29, 2016}}</ref> The second episode, "Founder's Mutation", was viewed by 9.67 million.<ref name=miniratings2/>

==Future==
In an interview with ''[[Entertainment Weekly]]'', Duchovny mentioned that, if the season were successful, he would be interested in filming another: "I would be open to doing another cycle. I don't know that I could do a 20-episode version of this show at this point in my life, and I don't know that Gillian could. But I think everybody is open ended on what happens after this. Certainly, we didn't bring it back with the idea of ending it."<ref>{{cite magazine |last1=Hibberd |first1=James |title=''The X-Files'': David Duchovny Says the New Script Made Him Cry |url=https://www.ew.com/article/2015/05/26/x-files-david-duchovny |magazine=[[Entertainment Weekly]] |access-date=October 1, 2015 |date=May 26, 2015}}</ref> At the 2016 [[Television Critics Association]] panel for the series, Carter stated, "If we do well in the ratings, I can't imagine we wouldn't be asked to do more."<ref>{{cite magazine |url=https://www.ew.com/article/2016/01/15/x-files-tca |title=''X-Files'' Creator Admits Second Movie Was a Misstep |magazine=Entertainment Weekly |date=January 15, 2016 |access-date=January 17, 2016 |last=Hibberd |first=James}}</ref> 

Fox Television Group chairman and CEO Gary Newman stated that he and fellow executive Dana Walden would be open to another renewal, stating, "We would love to do this again, so we'd be on board if schedules can be worked out."<ref>{{cite web |url=https://variety.com/2016/tv/news/the-x-files-revival-new-season-future-show-renew-chances-1201680907/ |title='The X-Files' Creator Says Revival Is a Chance to 'Prove That the Show Has More Life' In It |work=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]] |first=Laura |last=Prudom |date=January 15, 2016 |access-date=January 27, 2016}}</ref> In an interview with ''[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]'' prior to the premiere, Anderson, Duchovny, and Walden stated their willingness for another renewal.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://variety.com/2016/tv/features/x-files-revival-fox-david-duchovny-gillian-anderson-1201682379/ |title='The X-Files': How Fox Revived Mulder and Scully's Search for the Truth |work=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]] |first=Geoff |last=Berkshire |date=January 19, 2016 |access-date=February 4, 2016}}</ref> On April 20, 2017, Fox  announced that ''The X-Files'' would be returning for an eleventh season, with ten episodes, to air in the [[2017–18 United States network television schedule|2017–18 television season]], after filming in mid-2017.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://deadline.com/2017/04/x-files-returns-event-series-fox-1202073290/ |title='The X-Files' Coming Back Again For New Event Series Next Season |website=Deadline Hollywood |first=Dominic |last=Patten |date=April 20, 2017 |access-date=April 21, 2017}}</ref>

==Home media release==
The season was released on Blu-ray and DVD in region 1 in June 2016. Special features include deleted and extended scenes; a gag reel; several featurettes – "The Makings of a Struggle", "Season X: An In-Depth Behind-the-Scenes Look at ''The Event Series''", "Monsters of the Week: A Recap from the Wildest and Scariest from the Original Series", "''The X-Files'' – Green Production PSA" and "Short Film – ''Grace'' by Karen Nielsen". There were three audio commentaries – "Founder's Mutation" with Chris Carter and James Wong, "Mulder & Scully Meet the Were-Monster" with David Duchovny, Gillian Anderson, Kumail Nanjiani and Darin Morgan and "My Struggle II" with Chris Carter and Gabe Rotter.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.tvshowsondvd.com/news/X-Files-The-Event-Series/22172 |title=The X-Files - Fox Press Release Sets a Date for 'The Event Series,' New 'Complete Series' Blu-ray |website=TVShowsOnDVD.com |first=David |last=Lambert |date=April 12, 2016 |access-date=April 14, 2016 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160415143836/http://www.tvshowsondvd.com/news/X-Files-The-Event-Series/22172 |archive-date=April 15, 2016 |df=mdy-all}}</ref>
